title: Researcher or academic
summary: For researchers: what you work on in plain words, selected publications, your identifiers, and how to collaborate or apply to work with you.

cards.purpose: What they work on, in words a non-specialist understands.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a square photo or logo for your profile picture?
slots.write: The member uploads it in the editor; never fetch one from the web.

slots.ask: What do you study, in a sentence a curious non-specialist would understand? What is your position and group?
slots.write: One plain-language paragraph, then bold-labelled affiliation and group lines exactly as the institution lists them.

slots.ask: Which five to ten publications should be listed? DOIs or links are enough; I'll copy the details.
slots.write: tag = venue · year (or Preprint · year); title exactly as published; description = authors in the venue's format, theirs included. Link the DOI.

slots.ask: Are you recruiting students or postdocs, or open to collaboration?
slots.write: Text = what is open and from when, as on the official advert. Institutional email only if they want it shown. Only an address they confirm may be public: everyone can see it.

slots.ask: Which scholarly profiles should be linked: ORCID, Google Scholar, institutional page, code?
Any talks or courses you want to list?
slots.write: tag = type · year; title as given; description = event and city.
